title: fix(plugin-kanban): the swimlane region owns the vertical scroll, and the column header sticks (objectui#8449)
body:
Fixes #8449

Implements the ruling in comment 5597654059: **option A — the swimlane region scrolls, and the column-header row sticks to the top of it.**

## What changed

`packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx`, swimlane layout only, two class lists:

| element | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| swimlane region | `py-3 sm:py-4 min-w-0 overflow-hidden` | `pb-3 sm:pb-4 min-w-0 overflow-x-hidden overflow-y-auto` |
| column-header row | `flex shrink-0 … pl-36 sm:pl-44 overflow-x-auto` | `flex shrink-0 … pl-36 sm:pl-44 pt-3 sm:pt-4 overflow-x-auto sticky top-0 z-10 bg-background` |

The region already had a bounded height and already zeroed its own automatic minimum size — `overflow-hidden` is a scroll container too. It was throwing the overflow away instead of offering it. `overflow-y-auto` is the whole scroll fix; `overflow-x` stays `hidden` so this does not become a second horizontal scroller competing with the one axis objectui#8448 settled.

**The `pt-*` move is browser-measured, not taste.** A scroll container's padding lives inside its scrollport, so content scrolls through it: with `py-*` left on the region the pinned header stuck at `region.top + 16` and a 16px band of the previous lane's cards stayed visible ABOVE the frozen titles. Carried onto the header row, that band is painted by the row's own opaque background. The region keeps `pb-*`, which nothing scrolls past. The `pl-*` indent objectui#7303's pin compares is untouched.

## The card's measurement, inverted — in a real browser

Chromium 1194 at 1600x1000, real Tailwind CSS, the real `object-kanban` board mounted in a height-bounded pane (six swimlanes, five columns), **driven with `page.mouse.wheel` through the browser's input pipeline**.

⚠️ Read that last clause: `element.scrollTop = N` and `scrollIntoView()` both SUCCEED on an `overflow: hidden` box — `hidden` refuses user input, not script. A first pass built on those reported "6/6 lanes reachable" on the broken build, i.e. the bug reported as fixed. Every reachability number below is wheel-driven.

The control is the same page with the pre-fix CSS forced back on (`overflow: hidden` on the region, `position: static` and no background on the header row), so each number is read twice off one DOM:

```
                              FIXED            DEFECT (control)
region overflow-y             auto             hidden
region scrollHeight/client    1475 / 1000      1475 / 1000
document scrollable           false            false
wheel x12  -> region.scrollTop  475              0        <- the defect, lit
lanes in view at rest         ann bob cai dee  ann bob cai dee
lanes in view after wheel     cai dee eve fay  ann bob cai dee
header position               sticky           static
header offset from region top   0 at rest,       0 at rest,
                                0 scrolled      -459 scrolled
header row height             40               40         (24 content + its own pt-4)
header background             rgb(246,246,249) rgba(0,0,0,0)
column title wins hit test    true             false
```

⇒ **acceptance met**: with the lanes overflowing, a wheel reaches the full 475px of overflow and lanes 5 and 6 (`eve`, `fay`) come into view; the column titles stay pinned at offset 0, at height 40 (not the height 0 objectui#7303 closed), opaque, and still winning their own hit test with lane cards passing behind them.

⚠️ **Urgency input the card asked for, as far as it can honestly be taken here.** I did not measure real boards' lane cardinality — that needs production data. What this fixture does say: at 1600x1000 with two cards per cell, **4 of 6 lanes fit**, so any grouping field with five or more distinct values put content out of reach. Grouping by owner or account is far past that.

## objectui#7303's pin — the guard on this work, unweakened

Not touched, and deliberately re-read from the new pin: `position: sticky` does NOT remove a box from flow, so the header row is still a shrinkable-in-principle flex item that is also a scroll container, and `shrink-0` is still what keeps it out of the shrink pool. Ablation leg C below deletes `shrink-0` and reddens objectui#7303's pin and this PR's, together.

## Tests

New: `packages/plugin-kanban/src/__tests__/swimlaneVerticalScroll-8449.test.tsx` (3 cases).

⚠️ **What it does and does not claim.** Vitest runs in happy-dom, which performs no layout and applies no CSS: `scrollHeight`, `clientHeight`, `getBoundingClientRect()` and `position: sticky` are indistinguishable between the broken build, the fixed build, and a board that never rendered. **No geometry is asserted there** — that would be a pin that cannot fail. The geometry is the browser table above, exactly as objectui#7303's and objectui#8448's pins document for this surface. The file pins the class contract that DECIDES that geometry, as invariants rather than spellings: the region's effective `overflow-y` must be a scrolling value; the board root must still be height-bounded (dropping it is refused arm B arriving by the back door); the header row must be the region's first child, sticky, with an inset, with an opaque background, and still out of the shrink pool; and the region must NOT become a horizontal scroll container, with objectui#8448's propagation re-driven to prove the axis survived.

**Ablation — every pin proven able to fail.** Each leg mutates the committed source, proves the mutation reached disk (old-anchor count to 0, new text present, on-disk blob hash printed), runs the pins, then restores from `HEAD` and proves the restore by blob hash plus an empty `git diff HEAD`:

```
leg A  region back to overflow-hidden       -> 1 failed | 2 passed   ("expected 'hidden' to match /^(auto|scroll)$/")
leg B  header loses sticky/top-0/bg         -> 1 failed | 2 passed   ("the column-header row must stick to the top…")
leg C  header loses shrink-0                -> 2 failed | 3 passed   (objectui#7303's pin AND this PR's, together)
control  unmutated tree                     -> 5 passed
```

**Gates, all green, all read from the gate's own verdict line:**

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-kanban/         38 files, 244 tests passed
pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban type-check    exit 0  (tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json — the test file IS covered)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban lint          0 errors, 180 warnings (all pre-existing house pattern)
node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs            OK — 1 changeset for 1 released package
pnpm check:control-bytes                             OK (6996 tracked text files)
pnpm changeset:check / check:self-import / check:unreferenced-sources   OK
node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test   NOT GOVERNED (3 paths, 0 matches)
```

Read at `57d6f288a`. Repo-wide `turbo run lint` and the full suite are CI's; the affected package's own lint and test units were run whole, not narrowed.

## Not in scope, deliberately

- **Filed as #8797** — while measuring the horizontal axis I found the header row's max `scrollLeft` is **288** against the lane rows' **298** (the lane rows carry `px-2` the header row does not). Scrolled fully right, the sync clamps at the header's smaller maximum and every title sits **9px** off its column; 1px everywhere else in the range. Same family as objectui#8448, different cause, and objectui#8448's pin cannot see it because it asserts propagation, not range. Dedup was run and returned a **lit** reading (objectui#8449, #8448, #7303, #8508 — every adjacent card, none of them this), not a zero.
- The `pl-36 sm:pl-44` indent with nothing rendered in it is still there, still scrolling away with the content. Carried forward from objectui#8448 as out of scope, and it is the thing a sticky-lane-label change would want.

## 验收备注

- noted, not filed: the header row now measures **40** tall where objectui#7303's docblock records **24**. Nothing regressed — the extra 16 is the row's own `pt-4`, and the content is still 24 — but anyone re-running that out-of-band measurement should expect the new number.
- noted, not filed: `z-10` on the header row is defensive against dnd-kit's drag transforms painting over a sticky sibling. Not observed failing without it; it was not worth a mid-drag measurement to find out.
